review_notes: I read the whole file. The only new concept is `Module.IsPseudoNull`, defined as `∀ p, height ≤ 1 → p ∉ Module.support R M`. I searched Mathlib for "pseudo-null" (case-insensitive) and found nothing. The definition is built on Mathlib's `Module.support`, `Ideal.height` and `LocalizedModule`. The lemmas reuse Mathlib's `Module.support_subset_of_injective`, `Module.support_subset_of_surjective`, `Module.support_of_exact`, `Module.notMem_support_iff` and `LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ`. They are not competing versions of existing concepts. The `LinearEquiv.isPseudoNull_iff` lemma is a standalone theorem about this predicate, not a duplicate concept. The only other uses I found are inside the same library (`PseudoIsomorphism/LinearMap.lean` and docs). I found no competing definition in the other Formal Frontier libraries.
